verses.1: As for every command that I am commanding you, you must be careful to observe it; do not add anything to it, nor subtract anything from it.
verses.2: If there arises in your midst a prophet or a dreamer of dreams, and they give you a sign or a wonder,
verses.3: and the sign or the wonder comes to pass, as they spoke to you, saying, "Let us go after other gods, whom you have not known, and let us serve them,"
verses.4: you must not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams. For it is the Lord your God who is testing you, to know whether you truly love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
verses.5: You shall follow the Lord your God, and you shall fear Him, keeping His commandments, listening to His voice, and serving Him, and clinging to Him.
verses.6: That prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, because they have spoken falsehood against the Lord your God, the One who brought you out of the land of Egypt and delivered you from the house of slavery, to turn you aside from the path that the Lord your God commanded you to walk in. You must purge the evil from among you.
verses.7: If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter, or the wife of your innermost being, or your closest friend, secretly entices you, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods, which you have not known, neither you nor your ancestors,
verses.8: gods of the peoples who are around you, whether near to you or far away, from one end of the earth to the other,"
verses.9: you must not show mercy toward them, nor listen to them, nor spare them, nor conceal them.
verses.10: You must surely put him to death, with your own hand you must be the first to strike him, and the hand of all the people the last.
verses.11: You must stone him to death, because he has tried to turn you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.
verses.12: Every Israelite must hear and fear, and no longer do among you this evil thing.
verses.13: If you hear in one of your cities, the one that the Lord your God gives you to dwell in,
verses.14: that certain wicked men have gone out from among you and enticed the inhabitants of their city, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods, which you have not known,"
verses.15: then you must investigate and inquire thoroughly. And if the matter is true and the abomination has indeed taken place among you,
verses.16: you must strike down the inhabitants of that city with the sword. You must devote it to destruction, along with all that is in it, and its livestock, with the sword.
verses.17: You must gather all its plunder in the middle of its square and burn the city and all its plunder with fire as a whole burnt offering to the Lord your God. And it shall become a perpetual ruin, never to be rebuilt again.
verses.18: And no portion of the devoted things may cling to your hand, so that the Lord may turn from His anger, and show you mercy, and have mercy on you, and multiply you as He swore to your ancestors.
verses.19: For if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to keep all His commandments that I command you today, to do what is right in the eyes of the Lord your God.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: The phrasing "you must be careful to observe it" reflects the imperative to keep the commandments precisely as given.
- v. 4: "It is the Lord your God who is testing you" follows a causal interpretation of the Hebrew text, which reads as "for it is testing."
- v. 10: The Hebrew uses "yad kha" ("your hand") and "yad kol ha'am" ("the hand of all the people") to distinguish roles in the execution, which is preserved in the English.
- v. 16: "Whole burnt offering" is used for "khalil," which refers to a complete or undivided offering.
- v. 17: "Kavod" and similar nuances are not present in this chapter and thus no special note is required.
